Interface Definition Documentation

 interface svt_mipi_cphy_if ()
General Description

This interface defines a CPHY interface used by the SVT CPHY Transactor to hold an instance of CPHY signal interface that can be used for communication with a DUT.

This interface has mutiple modports defined considering Transmitter or Receiver direction in HS/LP mode.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about. Note that all other signals or registers within this interface can and should be ignored (they are VIP and/or interface internal control signals).

Required Interface Connections: The following CPHY interface signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

Signal Name Signal Description
Trios Interface Signals
A Corresponds to line A in a CPHY Lane
B Corresponds to line B in a CPHY Lane
C Corresponds to line C in a CPHY Lane
Clock Interface Signals
hs_tx_clk Transmitter high speed clock.
hs_rx_clk Recovered/testbench provided high speed clock.
lp_tx_clk Transmitter low power escape mode clock.
lp_rx_clk Receiver low power recovered escape mode clock.
Status Interface Signals
hs_xmtr_enable Indicates respective CPHY HS transmitter is Enabled/Disabled.
signal_direction Indicates current CPHY(Master/Slave) signal direction.

Debug Interface:

The following signals are available to help debug the CPHY modules

Signal Name Signal Description
Transmitter Side Debug Interface Signals
word_data Indicates transmitter’s present word data.
wire_state Indicates transmitter’s present wire state.
symbol Indicates transmitter’s present symbol value.
fsm_state Indicates transmitter’s present FSM state.
Receiver Side Debug Interface Signals
rcvr_word_data Indicates receiver’s present word data.
rcvr_wire_state Indicates receiver’s present wire state.
rcvr_symbol Indicates receiver’s present symbol value.
rcvr_fsm_state Indicates receiver’s present FSM state.

 interface svt_mipi_cphy_ppi_if ()
General Description

This interface defines a CPHY PPI interface used by the SVT CPHY PPI Transactor to hold an instance of CPHY PPI interface that can be used for communication with a DUT.

This interface has multiple modports defined considering Transmitter or Receiver direction in HS/LP mode.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about. Note that all other signals or registers within this interface can and should be ignored (they are VIP and/or interface internal control signals).

Required Interface Connections: The following CPHY PPI interface signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

Signal Name Signal Description
Clock Interface Signals
tx_symbol_clk_hs Transmitter high speed symbol clock.
tx_word_clk_hs Transmitter generated/testbench provided high speed word clock.
rx_word_clk_hs Receiver recovered/testbench provided high speed word clock.
tx_clk_esc Transmitter escape mode clock.
rx_clk_esc Receiver recovered/testbench generated escape mode clock.
High Speed Transmit Interface Signals
tx_request_hs Indicates transmit request for HS transmitter.
tx_data_width_hs Indicates data width 16 or 32 bit for HS transmitter.
tx_word_valid_hs Indicates word [1:0] validity for HS transmitter.
tx_data_hs Indicates data for HS transmitter.
tx_send_sync_hs Indicates sync word information for HS transmitter.
tx_ready_hs Indicates data acknowledgement for HS transmitter.
High Speed Receive Interface Signals
rx_active_hs Indicates active transaction for HS receiver.
rx_data_width_hs Indicates data width 16 or 32 bit for HS receiver.
rx_valid_hs Indicates word [1:0] validity for HS receiver.
rx_data_hs Indicates data for HS receiver.
rx_sync_hs Indicates sync word information for HS receiver.
rx_invalid_code_hs Indicates invalid code received for HS receiver.
Escape Mode Transmit Interface Signals
tx_request_esc Indicates escape request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_lpdt_esc Indicates lpdt request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_data_esc Indicates lpdt data for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_valid_esc Indicates lpdt data validity for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ready_esc Indicates lpdt data acknowledgement for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ulps_esc Indicates ulps request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_ulps_exit Indicates ulps exit request for Tx Escape Mode.
tx_trigger_esc Indicates trigger request for Tx Escape Mode.
Escape Mode Receive Interface Signals
rx_lpdt_esc Indicates lpdt request for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_data_esc Indicates lpdt data for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_valid_esc Indicates lpdt data validity for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_ulps_esc Indicates ulps request for Rx Escape Mode.
rx_trigger_esc Indicates trigger request for Rx Escape Mode.
Control Interface Signals
enable Indicates to enable the PPI interface.
direction Indicates transmit/receive direction.
turn_request Indicates turn-around request.
turn_disable Indicates turn-around disable.
force_rx_mode Indicates force into receive mode/ wait for stop state.
force_tx_stop_mode Indicates force into transmit mode/ generate stop state.
stop_state Indicates in stop state.
ulps_active_not Indicates ulps state not active.
Error Interface Signals
err_sot_hs Indicates start of transmission (SoT) error.
err_sot_sync_hs Indicates start of transmission synchronization error.
err_esc Indicates escape entry error.
err_sync_esc Indicates low power data transmission synchronization error.
err_control Indicates control error.
err_contention_lp0 Indicates lp0 contention error.
err_contention_lp1 Indicates lp1 contention error.

Debug Interface:

The following signals are available to help debug the CPHY PPI modules

Signal Name Signal Description
Transmitter Side Debug Interface Signals
xmtr_fsm_state Indicates transmitter’s present FSM state.
Receiver Side Debug Interface Signals
rcvr_fsm_state Indicates receiver’s present FSM state.
passive_rcvr_fsm_state Indicates passive receiver’s present FSM state.

 interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_clock_ref ()
General Description

This interface includes the reference clock signals used by driver for driving clock lane and data lane. This signal should be connected to the respective clock generator or testbench clocks.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following serial clock reference signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    TxDDRClkHD_I In Phase Reference DDR clock
    TxDDRClkHD_Q Quadrature Phase Reference DDR clock
    TxClkEsc Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • In Phase DDR Clock - TxDDRClkHD_I signal is used to transmit High-Speed data bits over the Lane Interconnect.

  • Quadrature Phase DDR Clock - TxDDRClkHD_Q signal is used to generate High-Speed Clock signal over the Lane Interconnect.The TxDDRClkHD_Q (quadrature) clock signal is phase shifted from the TxDDRClkHD-I clock signal.

  • Escape mode Reference clock - TxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences .

logic
TxDDRClkHD_I

TxDDRClkHD_Q

 interface svt_mipi_dphy_ppi_dut_phy_rx_if ()
General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by PPI Receiver.

This interface defines D-PHY DUT PHY(PPI) parallel Unidirectional Receiver Interaface

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to receive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 Appendix A.

Modports

  • rx_port Port used by receiver to receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    RxByteClkHS High speed receive byte clock
    RxClkEsc Rx Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Receiver byte clock - For RxByteClkHS signal, the DUT is expected to provide the VIP with an high speed byte clock to allow vip to receiver data on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataHS, RxValidHS, RxActiveHS and RxSyncHS drives on rising edge of RxByteClkHS

  • Low power Receiver clock - RxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences. It is a clock for low power data to be receive on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataEsc, RxValidEsc, RxLpdtEsc, RxUlpsEsc and RxTriggerEsc drives on rising edge of RxClkEsc

 interface svt_mipi_dphy_ppi_dut_phy_tx_if ()
General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by PPI Transmitter.

This interface defines D-PHY DUT PHY(PPI) Unidirectional Transmit Interafce
This inteface defines modports and clocking blocks to drive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 Appendix A.

Modports:

  • tx_port Port used by driver to drive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    TxByteClkHS High speed transmit byte clock
    TxClkEsc Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Transmitter byte clock - For TxByteClkHS signal, the DUT is expected to provide the VIP with an high speed byte clock to allow vip to transmit data on lane interconnect. All signals TxDataHS, TxRequestHS , TxSkewCalHS, TxSkewCalInitHS and TxReadyHS drives on rising edge of TxByteClkHS

  • Low power Transmitter clock - TxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences. It is a clock for low power data to be transmitted on lane interconnect. All signals TxDataEsc, TxValidEsc, TxReadyEsc drives on rising edge of TxClkEsc

 interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_rx_if ()
General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.00.00.

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by D-PHY Receiver.

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to receive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.00.00.

Modports

  • rx_port Port used by receiver to receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    dp External dp line for connection to Transmitter or Receiver.
    dn External dn line for connection to Transmitter or Receiver.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Receiver clock - On the hs_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to receive high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

 interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_txrx_if ()
General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1 .

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by bidirectional lanes only.

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to drive transaction on bidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1

Modports:

  • txrx_port Port used by driver to drive and receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    dp External dp line for connection to host or peripheral.
    dn External dn line for connection to host or peripheral.
    dpin Connected to dp external line when enable is 1.
    dnin Connected to dn external line when enable is 1.
    dpout Connected to dp external line when enable is 0.
    dnout Connected to dn external line when enable is 0.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Transmitter clock - On the hs_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to transmit high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Transmitter clock - On the lp_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock to transmit escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

  • High Speed Receiver clock - On the hs_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to receive high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Receiver clock - On the lp_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock signals(dp^dn) to receive escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

 interface svt_mipi_dsi_device_serial_if ()
General Description

This interface defines the MIPI DSI device Serial interface which is a subinterface for DSI device interface.

This interface defines following sub-interfaces require for DSI device serial transmission.

  • Serial Reference clock interface This svt_mipi_dphy_serial_clock_ref sub-interface includes signals used as a reference clock. This signals should be connected to the clocks generated by clock generator or testbench.
  • Serial Rx Clock interface This sub-inteface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_rx_if defines the clock lane for clock transmission during data transaction.
  • Serial Lane0 interface This sub-interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_txrx_if defines the Lane 0 bidirectional interface for transmission and reception of the transaction.
  • Serial Rx interface This sub-interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_rx_if defines the Lane 1 to 3 unidirectional interface for reception of the transaction.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Transmit clock - On the hs_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input DDR clock to transmit high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Transmit clock - On the lp_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock to transmit escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

  • High Speed Receive clock - On the hs_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to receive high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

 interface svt_mipi_dsi_host_if ()
General Description

This interface defines the MIPI DSI Host interface used by the SVT DSI Transactor to communicate with a DUT.

It supports following interfaces:

  • DSI host Serial interface It defines DSI host D-PHY serial svt_mipi_dsi_host_serial_if interface with differential clock and data lanes. It defines one clock, one bidirectional lane (Lane 0) and three unidirectional data lanes (Lane 1 to 3 : Tx).
  • DSI host DUT PHY interface It defines DSI host D-PHY PPI Parallel interface svt_mipi_dsi_host_ppi_dut_phy_if with Data lanes, Control and Error signals. It defines four data lanes (Lane 0 : Tx/Rx, Lane 1 to 3 : Tx).

1)svt_mipi_dsi_host_serial_if ::

General Description

This interface defines the MIPI DSI host Serial interface which is a subinterface for DSI host interface.

This interface defines following sub-interfaces require for DSI host serial transmission.

  • Serial Reference clock interface This svt_mipi_dphy_serial_clock_ref sub-interface includes signals used as a reference clock. This signals should be connected to the clocks generated by clock generator or testbench.
  • Serial Tx Clock interface This sub-inteface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_tx_if defines the clock lane for clock transmission during data transaction.
  • Serial Lane0 interface This sub-interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_txrx_if defines the Lane 0 bidirectional interface for transmission and reception of the transaction.
  • Serial Tx interface This sub-interface svt_mipi_dphy_serial_tx_if defines the Lane 1 to 3 unidirectional interface for transmission of the transaction.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Transmit clock - On the hs_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input DDR clock to transmit high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Transmit clock - On the lp_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock to transmit escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

  • High Speed Receive clock - On the hs_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to receive high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Receive clock - On the lp_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock signals(dp^dn) to receive escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

svt_mipi_dphy_serial_clock_ref ::

General Description

This interface includes the reference clock signals used by driver for driving clock lane and data lane. This signal should be connected to the respective clock generator or testbench clocks.

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following DSI serial clock reference signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    TxDDRClkHD_I In Phase Reference DDR clock
    TxDDRClkHD_Q Quadrature Phase Reference DDR clock
    TxClkEsc Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • In Phase DDR Clock - TxDDRClkHD_I signal is used to transmit High-Speed data bits over the Lane Interconnect.

  • Quadrature Phase DDR Clock - TxDDRClkHD_Q signal is used to generate High-Speed Clock signal over the Lane Interconnect.The TxDDRClkHD_Q (quadrature) clock signal is phase shifted from the TxDDRClkHD-I clock signal.

  • Escape mode Reference clock - TxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences . Escape mode sequences consists of ULPM(Ultra Low power mode), TRIGGER and LPDT(Low Power Data Transmission) for DSI.

svt_mipi_dphy_serial_tx_if ::

General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification as being (potentially) included in a DSI .

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by DSI.

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to drive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1.

Modports:

  • tx_port Port used by driver to drive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    dp External dp line for connection to host or peripheral.
    dn External dn line for connection to host or peripheral.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed transmit clock - On the hs_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to transmit high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power transmit clock - On the lp_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock to transmit escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

svt_mipi_dphy_serial_txrx_if ::

General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1 .

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by bidirectional lanes only.

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to drive transaction on bidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1

Modports:

  • txrx_port Port used by driver to drive and receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    dp External dp line for connection to host or peripheral.
    dn External dn line for connection to host or peripheral.
    dpin Connected to dp external line when enable is 1.
    dnin Connected to dn external line when enable is 1.
    dpout Connected to dp external line when enable is 0.
    dnout Connected to dn external line when enable is 0.

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Transmit clock - On the hs_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input DDR clock to transmit high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Transmit clock - On the lp_tx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock to transmit escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

  • High Speed Receive clock - On the hs_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an high speed input clock to receive high speed data bits over the lane interconnect.

  • Low power Receive clock - On the lp_rx_clock signal, VIP will generate an low power input clock signals(dp^dn) to receive escape mode data or sequences over the lane interconnect.

svt_mipi_dphy_ppi_dut_phy_tx_if ::

General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification as being (potentially) included in a DSI .

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by DSI.

This interface defines D-PHY DUT PHY(PPI) parallel Unidirectional Transmit interface.

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to drive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 Appendix A.

Modports:

  • tx_port Port used by driver to drive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    TxByteClkHS High speed transmit byte clock
    TxClkEsc Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed transmit byte clock - For TxByteClkHS signal, the DUT is expected to provide the VIP with an high speed byte clock to allow vip to transmit data on lane interconnect. All signals TxDataHS, TxRequestHS and TxReadyHS drives on rising edge of TxByteClkHS

  • Low power transmit clock - TxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences. It is a clock for low power data to be transmitted on lane interconnect. All signals TxDataEsc, TxValidEsc, TxReadyEsc drives on rising edge of TxClkEsc

svt_mipi_dphy_ppi_dut_phy_rx_if::

General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1.

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by PPI Receiver.

This interface defines D-PHY DUT PHY(PPI) parallel Unidirectional Receiver Interaface

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to receive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 Appendix A.

Modports

  • rx_port Port used by receiver to receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    RxByteClkHS High speed receive byte clock
    RxClkEsc Rx Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Receiver byte clock - For RxByteClkHS signal, the DUT is expected to provide the VIP with an high speed byte clock to allow vip to receiver data on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataHS, RxValidHS, RxActiveHS and RxSyncHS drives on rising edge of RxByteClkHS

  • Low power Receiver clock - RxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences. It is a clock for low power data to be receive on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataEsc, RxValidEsc, RxLpdtEsc, RxUlpsEsc and RxTriggerEsc drives on rising edge of RxClkEsc

General Description

This SystemVerilog 'interface' definition declares all of the signals (scoped within an instance of this interface) that are specified by the D-PHY Specification v1.1.

The interface declares 'clocking blocks' that define the clock synchronization and directionality of interface signals and declares 'modports' (which reference the clocking blocks) that are to be used by PPI Receiver.

This interface defines D-PHY DUT PHY(PPI) parallel Unidirectional Receiver Interaface

This interface defines modports and clocking blocks to receive transaction on unidirectional differential lane as per MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 Appendix A.

Modports

  • rx_port Port used by receiver to receive the data transaction
  • monitor_port Port used by monitor to sample the data transaction

Interface Connections

Following are descriptions of the interface connections users need to be concerned about.

  • Required Interface Connections: The following signals are expected to be connected within the testbench.

    Signal Name Signal Description
    RxByteClkHS High speed receive byte clock
    RxClkEsc Rx Escape mode Reference clock

Usage Notes

Following is important usage information concerning the use of this interface.

  • High Speed Receiver byte clock - For RxByteClkHS signal, the DUT is expected to provide the VIP with an high speed byte clock to allow vip to receiver data on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataHS, RxValidHS, RxActiveHS and RxSyncHS drives on rising edge of RxByteClkHS

  • Low power Receiver clock - RxClkEsc signal is used to generate escape mode sequences. It is a clock for low power data to be receive on lane interconnect. All signals RxDataEsc, RxValidEsc, RxLpdtEsc, RxUlpsEsc and RxTriggerEsc drives on rising edge of RxClkEsc

 svt_mipi_dsi_host_serial_if  attribute
 svt_mipi_dsi_host_if::serial_if

D-PHY Serial Interface
D-PHY serial interface uses the signals based on the MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1.

It includes 1 clock lane and 4 data lane differential interfaces

It also includes reference clock interface to connect the reference clock generated from clock generator.

 svt_mipi_dsi_host_ppi_dut_phy_if  attribute
 svt_mipi_dsi_host_if::dut_phy_if

DUT PHY(PPI) Interface
D-PHY PPI Parallel interface uses the signals based on the MIPI D-PHY specification v1.1 - Appendix A.

It includes 1 clock lane and 4 data lane differential interfaces

It also includes reference clock interface to connect the reference clock generated from clock generator.

 svt_mipi_dsi_device_serial_if  attribute
 svt_mipi_dsi_device_if::serial_if

DPhy Serial Interface
DPhy serial interface uses the signals based on the MIPI DPhy specification v1.1.

It includes 1 clock lane and 4 data lane differential interfaces

It also includes reference clock interface to connect the reference clock generated from clock generator.
